highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should be aware of this release as it may unlock more powerful reasoning and coding capabilities within their workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.232: Subagent Forking On by Default & Cross-Session Mentions
highlights.summary: Subagent forking is now enabled by default, meaning a fork-type subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache — great for parallelizing complex tasks. You can now also type @ in the prompt to mention and message another Claude session by name, enabling coordination across sessions.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.233: GitLab Merge Request Support & User Identity Forwarding
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports GitLab merge request URLs in the --worktree flag, with MRs displayed as !N in the agents view — a handy addition for teams using GitLab. An opt-in forward_user_identity setting is also available for Anthropic upstreams, useful for organizations routing traffic through a proxy.

highlights.title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic has introduced cross-session messaging, allowing you to send messages between different Claude Code sessions using the @ mention syntax. This is especially powerful for orchestrating multiple agents working on different parts of a project simultaneously.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Claude Code's Auto mode is now enabled by default, meaning Claude will automatically decide when to ask for confirmation versus act autonomously based on context. Beginners benefit from this change as it reduces friction and lets Claude handle more tasks end-to-end without constant prompting.

highlights.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic's official blog post offers practical guidance on getting the most out of Claude Code sessions, covering strategies around context management, task scoping, and prompt clarity. This is a must-read for developers looking to improve efficiency and reduce wasted tokens.

highlights.title: Learn 80% of Claude Code in 10 Minutes (2026 Tutorial)
highlights.summary: This concise YouTube tutorial promises to cover the most important Claude Code features in just 10 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a fast but comprehensive onboarding. It's a great starting point before diving into more advanced workflows.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: A 30-minute YouTube tutorial designed to take developers from basics to confident intermediate usage of Claude Code. It's a solid next step after introductory content, covering more advanced features and real-world use cases.

tips_of_the_day: Use the @ mention feature to send context or instructions from one Claude Code session to another — this lets you split a large project into parallel workstreams and have agents coordinate without manual copy-pasting.

Since Auto mode is now the default, review your project's CLAUDE.md file to clearly define boundaries for what Claude should and shouldn't do autonomously — good guardrails help Auto mode work safely and effectively.

When starting a long coding session, explicitly tell Claude the scope of the task upfront and break it into numbered steps — this helps Claude maintain focus, use the prompt cache more efficiently, and reduces mid-session drift.
